transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

If you can hear the motor running but the drum isn't moving, the most common cause on Hotpoint dryers is that the drive belt has snapped or slipped off the pulley. This disconnects the motor from the drum. To confirm this safely: please unplug the dryer first. Then try to turn the drum by hand. 1. If it spins very freely with no resistance at all, the belt is likely broken or off.
2. If it feels stiff, stuck, or makes a grinding noise, something may be jammed inside or the bearings are seized. Please let me know how it feels when you turn it by hand.
unplugged it and turned the drum by hand and it spins really easy almost no resistance at all

That suggests the drive belt has probably snapped or slipped off its pulley. This is a very common failure on Hotpoint dryers and explains why the motor runs but the drum doesn't move. It is usually on a sticker inside the door opening (or sometimes behind the small flap at the bottom front). What does it say?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
sticker is worn but it starts TVHM8 the rest i cant read. also i shone a torch through the filter slot and can see a black rubbery strip lying at the bottom

[Heading: Likely cause: drive belt]
That suggests it: the drive belt has snapped and fallen into the bottom of the drum or filter housing. To fix this, you will need to replace the drive belt. Since I cannot confirm the exact full model number from the worn sticker, please search for "Hotpoint TVHM8 dryer spare parts" online or contact a local appliance parts supplier with that partial code and your serial number (usually on a separate metal plate inside the door frame) to ensure you get the correct belt. The repair involves removing the top panel and the front bulkhead to access the drum, fitting the new belt around the drum and motor pulley, and reassembling. If you are not comfortable dismantling the machine, please call an engineer.

candidates: Drive belt has snapped or slipped off (high)
Jockey/idler pulley mechanism is stuck or broken (medium)
Drum obstruction or seized bearing (less likely if motor runs freely) (low)
